qualities.label: Focus

record.name: Lemon
record.description: Cold-pressed from lemon peel. Dominated by limonene, which gives it the sharp citrus character used across cleaning, fragrance, and flavor work.

precautions.legacySafety: Phototoxic on skin in sunlight; avoid undiluted topical use.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported calm quality: a small randomized study reported lower test-anxiety scores after a brief exposure to lemon essential-oil aroma than in its control group.
qualityMappings.limitations: 46 nursing students and one acute test setting. This is whole lemon oil, not isolated limonene; the result does not establish treatment of anxiety or lasting relaxation. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

record.name: Lavender
record.description: Steam-distilled from flowering tops. Linalool and linalyl acetate drive its well-studied calming profile.

constituents.basis: ISO 11024 specification cited in GC-MS study

precautions.legacySafety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported calm quality: a trial of lavender aromatherapy massage reported lower salivary cortisol immediately after treatment than usual care.
qualityMappings.limitations: Whole lavender oil was used with massage in 52 pregnant participants. There was no massage-only comparison, so the contribution of the oil cannot be separated from massage. Cortisol is not a direct measure of feeling calm. This does not establish safety during pregnancy. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Counterevidence for the purported calm quality: a randomized trial of a lavender, bergamot and cedarwood aroma mixture did not show benefit; the carrier-only group had lower anxiety scores than the fragrant groups at treatment completion.
qualityMappings.limitations: This was a multi-oil intervention in 313 radiotherapy patients. Its findings cannot be assigned to lavender alone or generalized to everyday cosmetic use. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported sleep / wind-down quality: a review combining 11 randomized trials reported better adult sleep-quality scores with lavender essential-oil interventions overall.
qualityMappings.limitations: Review of whole-oil interventions, not isolated linalool. Study quality, routes, concentrations and duration varied; some subgroup results were not significant. This does not establish treatment of insomnia or an effective spray formulation. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

precautions.legacySafety: Keep away from young children; can irritate eyes and mucous membranes.

qualityMappings.limitations: Single-session aroma exposure in healthy volunteers. This is whole-oil evidence, not a trial of isolated menthol, and does not establish improved everyday work or study performance. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.limitations: Mixed outcomes after a single brief exposure in healthy adults. Better results on some tasks do not establish general cognitive enhancement. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported focus quality: after rosemary whole-oil aroma exposure, blood 1,8-cineole levels correlated with performance on some cognitive tasks.
qualityMappings.limitations: Small correlational study of 20 volunteers. The exposure was whole rosemary oil; measuring one constituent does not establish that isolated 1,8-cineole caused the results, or that other oils containing it have the same effect. compounds.name: Limonene
compounds.description: The defining compound of citrus peels. One of the most abundant terpenes in nature and widely studied for mood, stress, and cleaning applications.

compounds.name: Linalool
compounds.description: The calming backbone of lavender. Among the most researched terpenes for relaxation and sleep-related outcomes.

compounds.name: Linalyl Acetate
compounds.description: A floral, fruity monoterpenoid that is also an acetate ester, reported in lavender and bergamot oils.

compounds.name: Menthol
compounds.description: Activates TRPM8 cold receptors, producing the cooling sensation. The signature compound of peppermint.

compounds.name: Menthone
compounds.description: Peppermint's secondary ketone; adds the sharp, fresh mint edge beneath menthol.

compounds.name: Eucalyptol (1,8-Cineole)
compounds.description: The penetrating compound in eucalyptus and rosemary. Studied for respiratory and anti-inflammatory applications.

compounds.name: Terpinen-4-ol
compounds.description: Tea tree's signature compound and the main driver of its documented antimicrobial activity.

compounds.name: Alpha-Pinene
compounds.description: The smell of pine forests. Common across conifers, frankincense, and rosemary; studied for alertness and respiratory effects.

compounds.name: Beta-Pinene
compounds.description: Alpha-pinene's close relative; contributes dry woody notes to citrus and conifer oils.

compounds.name: Beta-Caryophyllene
compounds.description: A dietary sesquiterpene (also in black pepper) notable for interacting with CB2 receptors. Found in clove, copaiba, and lavender.

compounds.name: Eugenol
compounds.description: A warm, spicy compound reported in clove bud oil. Long used in dentistry; potent, so dilution matters. Not a terpene: a phenylpropanoid.

compounds.name: Gamma-Terpinene
compounds.description: Common citrus and tea-tree constituent; contributes fresh herbal lift.

compounds.name: Alpha-Terpinene
compounds.description: Tea tree and citrus constituent with a warm woody-citrus character.

compounds.name: Alpha-Humulene
compounds.description: Sesquiterpene in clove and hops; adds earthy depth.

compounds.name: Myrcene
compounds.description: Common in citrus, hops, and cannabis; soft herbal-balsamic background note.

compounds.name: Citronellal
compounds.description: A lemon-scented monoterpenoid with an aldehyde group, reported in citronella and lemon eucalyptus oils.

compounds.name: Geraniol
compounds.description: Floral-rosy alcohol common in citronella, geranium, and palmarosa.

compounds.name: Thymol
compounds.description: Potent antimicrobial phenol; the signature compound of thyme oil.

compounds.name: Carvacrol
compounds.description: Oregano signature phenol with broad documented in-vitro antibacterial activity.

compounds.name: Cinnamaldehyde
compounds.description: A cinnamon-scented phenylpropanoid with an aldehyde group, reported in cinnamon bark oil.

compounds.name: Citral
compounds.description: A mixture of geranial and neral, two monoterpenoid aldehydes associated with the lemony aroma of lemongrass.

compounds.name: PMD (p-menthane-3,8-diol)
compounds.description: Refined from lemon eucalyptus citronellal. The botanical repellent compound with the strongest human trial evidence.

compounds.name: p-Cymene
compounds.description: A common aromatic monoterpene in oregano and thyme oils and a biosynthetic relative of carvacrol and thymol.

compounds.name: Furanoeudesma-1,3-diene

studies.title: Effects of citrus fragrance on immune function and depressive states
studies.authors: Komori T, Fujiwara R, Tanida M, Nomura J, Yokoyama MM
studies.finding: Citrus fragrance exposure was associated with normalized immune markers and reduced depressive scores in the study group.
studies.limitations: Small sample; early study design.

studies.title: Silexan, an orally administered Lavandula oil preparation, is effective in the treatment of subsyndromal anxiety disorder
studies.authors: Kasper S, Gastpar M, Muller WE, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender oil preparation showed anxiolytic effects in subsyndromal anxiety in a randomized controlled trial.
studies.limitations: Used a standardized oral preparation, not diffused oil.

studies.title: Melaleuca alternifolia (Tea Tree) Oil: a Review of Antimicrobial and Other Medicinal Properties
studies.authors: Carson CF, Hammer KA, Riley TV
studies.finding: Comprehensive review documenting tea tree oil's broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, attributed largely to terpinen-4-ol.
studies.limitations: Review of mostly in-vitro work; not clinical efficacy evidence.

studies.title: Anti-inflammatory activity of 1,8-cineol (eucalyptol) in bronchial asthma: a double-blind placebo-controlled trial
studies.authors: Juergens UR, Dethlefsen U, Steinkraus G, Gillissen A, Repges R, Vetter H
studies.finding: 1,8-cineole showed anti-inflammatory effects in asthma patients in a controlled trial setting.
studies.limitations: Tested isolated 1,8-cineole capsules, not eucalyptus oil.

studies.title: Beta-caryophyllene is a dietary cannabinoid
studies.authors: Gertsch J, Leonti M, Raduner S, et al.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.finding: Beta-caryophyllene was identified as a selective CB2 receptor agonist with anti-inflammatory effects in animal models.
studies.limitations: Animal and cell models; not human efficacy data.

studies.title: A Systematic Review of the Effect of Inhaled Essential Oils on Sleep
studies.authors: Lillehei AS, Halcon LL
studies.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
studies.finding: Across 15 studies, the majority reported improved sleep with inhaled essential oils, most commonly lavender, and no adverse events were reported.
studies.limitations: Small sample sizes across included studies; stronger study designs needed (per the authors).

studies.title: Peppermint Oil for the Treatment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
studies.authors: Khanna R, MacDonald JK, Levesque BG
studies.finding: Peppermint oil outperformed placebo for global IBS symptoms (RR 2.23) and abdominal pain (RR 2.14) across 726 patients, with mild transient adverse events.
studies.limitations: Substantial heterogeneity among trials; adverse events sparsely reported.

studies.title: A comparative study of tea-tree oil versus benzoylperoxide in the treatment of acne
studies.authors: Bassett IB, Pannowitz DL, Barnetson RS
studies.finding: Both 5% tea tree oil gel and 5% benzoyl peroxide significantly reduced inflamed and non-inflamed acne lesions over three months, with tea tree showing slower onset but fewer side effects.
studies.limitations: Single-blind design; older trial; acne lesion counts are observer-dependent.

studies.title: Comparative efficacy of insect repellents against mosquito bites
studies.authors: Fradin MS, Day JF
studies.finding: NEGATIVE RESULT for botanical repellents: citronella-based products protected for under 20 minutes versus 301.5 minutes for 23.8% DEET, leading the authors to conclude non-DEET products cannot be relied on for prolonged protection.
studies.limitations: Small human arm-exposure comparison of commercial products; short protection under these conditions is retained. Citronella-containing products do not authenticate a C. nardus-only oil or establish long-lasting protection.

studies.title: Effect of peppermint and eucalyptus oil preparations on neurophysiological and experimental algesimetric headache parameters
studies.authors: Göbel H, Schmidt G, Soyka D
studies.finding: Peppermint oil with ethanol significantly reduced headache sensitivity (analgesic effect), while the peppermint-eucalyptus-ethanol combination improved cognitive performance with a muscle-relaxing effect.
studies.limitations: Small sample (n=32); laboratory algesimetric measures rather than real-world headache outcomes.

studies.title: The effect of clove and benzocaine versus placebo as topical anesthetics
studies.authors: Alqareer A, Alyahya A, Andersson L
studies.finding: In 73 healthy volunteers, ground-clove gel and benzocaine reduced dental needle-insertion pain relative to placebo; the active groups did not differ significantly.
studies.limitations: A single buccal-mucosa application before a needle insertion. No essential-oil analgesia, toothache treatment or arbitrary topical formulation claim.
studies.material: Homemade ground-clove and glycerin gel; not distilled clove essential oil.

studies.title: Essential oils: their antibacterial properties and potential applications in foods—a review
studies.authors: Burt S
studies.finding: In vitro, thyme and oregano essential oils and their constituents (thymol, carvacrol, eugenol, cinnamaldehyde) inhibited Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli O157:H7 at 0.2–10 µl/ml, though higher concentrations were required in foods.
studies.limitations: Review of in-vitro work; food-matrix effects limit direct translation to products.

studies.title: Inhalation aromatherapy during radiotherapy: results of a placebo-controlled double-blind randomized trial
studies.authors: Graham PH, Browne L, Cox H, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: in 313 radiotherapy patients, inhaled aromatherapy (lavender/bergamot/cedarwood) did not significantly reduce anxiety or depression versus carrier-oil controls.
studies.limitations: Self-report outcome measures; radiotherapy setting may limit generalizability.

studies.title: Comparison of two topical preparations for the treatment of onychomycosis: Melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree) oil and clotrimazole
studies.authors: Buck DS, Nidorf DM, Addino JG
studies.finding: After 6 months of twice-daily application in 117 patients with culture-proven toenail onychomycosis, 100% tea tree oil and 1% clotrimazole produced comparable culture cure (TT 18%, CL 11%) and partial-or-full clinical resolution (TT 60%, CL 61%).
studies.limitations: High recurrence after treatment; no DOI on PubMed record; older trial.

studies.title: Repellency of oils of lemon eucalyptus, geranium, and lavender and the mosquito repellent MyggA natural to Ixodes ricinus (Acari: Ixodidae) in the laboratory and field
studies.authors: Jaenson TGT, Garboui S, Pålsson K
studies.finding: Lemon eucalyptus oil (C. citriodora, minimum 50% PMD) and lavender oil at 30% each showed 100% repellency against I. ricinus nymphs in lab bioassays, and 74–85% repellency on day 1 of field blanket-drag tests, declining to 42–45% by day 6.
studies.limitations: Field repellency declined over days; blanket-dragging is an indirect measure of human protection.

studies.title: A low-cost repellent for malaria vectors in the Americas: results of two field trials in Guatemala and Peru
studies.authors: Moore SJ, Darling ST, Sihuincha M, Padilla N, Devine GJ
studies.finding: A low-cost PMD/lemongrass-oil repellent gave over 98% protection for 5 hours in Guatemala and 95% for 6 hours in Peru, significantly exceeding the 15–20% DEET controls (92% and 64%) under high biting pressure.
studies.limitations: Single-night Latin-square trials per site; efficacy measured by landing counts, not malaria infection outcomes.

studies.title: Eco-Friendly Sanitization of Indoor Environments: Effectiveness of Thyme Essential Oil in Controlling Bioaerosol Levels and Disinfecting Surfaces
studies.authors: Sateriale D, Forgione G, De Cristofaro GA, Continisio L, Pagliuca C, Colicchio R, et al.
studies.finding: Aqueous thyme essential oil solutions (2.5% and 5%) applied by nebulization and direct contact reduced mesophilic and psychrophilic bacteria and environmental fungi in both air and on indoor surfaces.
studies.limitations: Indoor trial settings; long-term efficacy and cost-effectiveness not assessed.

studies.title: The Sleep-Enhancing Effect of Lavender Essential Oil in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
studies.authors: Shen H, Zhang LJ, Zhu WY
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials reported a statistically significant improvement in adult sleep quality associated with lavender essential-oil interventions.
studies.limitations: The authors noted limitations in the quantity and quality of included studies; interventions and routes varied.

studies.title: Eugenol as a promising antibiofilm and anti-quorum sensing agent: A systematic review
studies.authors: Ribeiro TAN, et al.
studies.finding: Systematic review of 14 eligible studies reported antibacterial, antibiofilm, anti-virulence and anti-quorum-sensing activity for eugenol across multiple bacterial strains.
studies.limitations: Predominantly laboratory evidence; does not establish clinical or finished-product efficacy.

studies.title: Antifungal activity of the clove essential oil from Syzygium aromaticum on Candida, Aspergillus and dermatophyte species
studies.authors: Pinto E, Vale-Silva L, Cavaleiro C, Salgueiro L
studies.finding: Clove essential oil and eugenol inhibited tested Candida, Aspergillus and dermatophyte strains; experiments implicated fungal membrane damage and reduced ergosterol.
studies.limitations: In-vitro study; results do not establish treatment efficacy in humans.

studies.title: Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Activities of Cinnamomum Sp. Essential Oil and Cinnamaldehyde: Antimicrobial Activities
studies.authors: Firmino DF, et al.
studies.finding: C. zeylanicum and C. cassia bark oils and cinnamaldehyde exhibited antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against tested bacterial biofilms.
studies.limitations: In-vitro concentrations and biofilm models do not establish efficacy of a consumer spray.

studies.title: Citrus limon Essential Oil: Chemical Composition and Selected Biological Properties Focusing on Antimicrobial, Antibiofilm, Insecticidal Activity and Preservative Effect
studies.authors: Kacaniova M, et al.
studies.finding: Lemon essential oil was characterized as 60.7% limonene, 12.6% beta-pinene and 10.3% gamma-terpinene and showed antimicrobial, antibiofilm and insecticidal activity in the reported laboratory and food-model assays.
studies.limitations: Laboratory and food-model evidence; composition is batch-specific and not a universal lemon-oil percentage.

studies.title: Boswellia Essential Oil: Natural Antioxidant as an Effective Antimicrobial and Anti-Inflammatory Agent
studies.authors: Obistioiu D, et al.
studies.finding: A commercial mixed-Boswellia essential oil dominated by alpha-pinene and limonene showed antimicrobial, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity in laboratory assays.
studies.limitations: Commercial mixture of several Boswellia species; laboratory evidence only.

studies.title: The anti-dermatophyte activity of Commiphora molmol
studies.authors: Mahboubi M, Mohammad Taghizadeh Kashani L
studies.finding: Commiphora molmol oil and a separate ethanol extract inhibited tested dermatophytes in vitro. Furanoeudesma-1,3-diene and menthofuran were major oil components; curzerene was described among major extract components.
studies.limitations: Oil and extract are separate materials. Laboratory fungal inhibition is not clinical skin treatment or wound-healing evidence.

studies.title: Inhibitory effect and mechanism of oregano essential oil on Listeria monocytogenes cells, toxins and biofilms
studies.authors: Guo P, et al.
studies.finding: Oregano essential oil inhibited L. monocytogenes in laboratory assays and reduced biofilm coverage on glass slides; mechanistic experiments implicated multiple cellular effects.
studies.limitations: Laboratory and food-model evidence; does not establish efficacy at consumer-product concentrations.

studies.authors: Moss M, Cook J, Wesnes K, Duckett P
studies.finding: Rosemary aroma significantly improved overall memory quality and secondary memory versus controls, while lavender impaired working memory and slowed reaction times on memory and attention tasks.
studies.limitations: Healthy young adults; single brief exposure; laboratory setting.
studies.title: Aromas of rosemary and lavender essential oils differentially affect cognition and mood in healthy adults

studies.authors: Chen PJ, Chou CC, Yang L, Tsai YL, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy massage lowered salivary cortisol and raised IgA immediately after treatment in pregnant women, with higher baseline IgA at 32 and 36 weeks versus study entry.
studies.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
studies.limitations: n=52; massage confound: aromatherapy massage compared against usual care, not massage alone.
studies.title: Effects of Aromatherapy Massage on Pregnant Women's Stress and Immune Function: A Longitudinal, Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial

studies.authors: Can Çiçek S, Demir Ş, Yılmaz D, Açıkgöz A, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy by inhalation and foot massage reduced blood pressure, heart rate, serum cortisol, and anxiety in patients with essential hypertension.
studies.limitations: Sample size not verifiable from abstract; single-center trial.
studies.title: The Effect of Aromatherapy on Blood Pressure and Stress Responses by Inhalation and Foot Massage in Patients With Essential Hypertension: Randomized Clinical Trial

studies.authors: Mori HM, Kawanami H, Kawahata H, Aoki M, et al.
studies.finding: Topical lavender oil accelerated wound closure in rats from day 4 to 10, increasing TGF-beta expression, fibroblast numbers, and type I and III collagen.
studies.limitations: Rat model; no human wound-healing data.
studies.title: Wound healing potential of lavender oil by acceleration of granulation and wound contraction through induction of TGF-β in a rat model

studies.authors: Schnitzler P, Schön K, Reichling J
studies.finding: Tea tree oil reduced HSV-1 and HSV-2 plaque formation by 98.2% and 93.0% at noncytotoxic concentrations, acting before or during viral adsorption; eucalyptus oil showed weaker activity.
studies.limitations: In-vitro cell culture only; active antiviral components unidentified.
studies.title: Antiviral activity of Australian tea tree oil and eucalyptus oil against herpes simplex virus in cell culture

studies.authors: Lee JH, Kim YG, Lee J, et al.
studies.finding: Carvacrol-rich oregano oil and thymol-rich thyme oil inhibited uropathogenic E. coli biofilm formation at subinhibitory concentrations and reduced fimbriae, swarming motility, and hemagglutination.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; no human or clinical data.
studies.title: Carvacrol-rich oregano oil and thymol-rich thyme red oil inhibit biofilm formation and the virulence of uropathogenic Escherichia coli

studies.authors: Kumar P, Mishra S, Malik A, Satya S, et al.
studies.finding: Peppermint oil was the most effective housefly repellent of six oils screened, and formulated peppermint and eucalyptus oils cut fly density 96-98% in field trials.
studies.limitations: Laboratory bioassays with limited field validation; not a human-use repellent trial.
studies.title: Repellent, larvicidal and pupicidal properties of essential oils and their formulations against the housefly, Musca domestica

studies.authors: Hur MH, Park J, Maddock-Jennings W, Kim DO, Lee MS
studies.finding: An essential-oil mouthwash (tea tree, peppermint, lemon) reduced oral malodour and volatile sulphur compounds in ICU patients significantly more than benzydamine at one hour.
studies.limitations: n=32; single ICU; follow-up only one hour.
studies.title: Reduction of mouth malodour and volatile sulphur compounds in intensive care patients using an essential oil mouthwash

studies.authors: Ball EL, Owen-Booth B, Gray A, Shenkin SD, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: across 12 included trials, the Cochrane reviewers found no convincing evidence that aromatherapy benefits people with dementia, with very low certainty throughout.
studies.limitations: Very low certainty evidence; inconsistent outcomes and poor harms reporting across trials.
studies.title: Aromatherapy for dementia

studies.authors: Kuriyama H, Watanabe S, Nakaya T, Shigemori I, et al.
studies.finding: Aromatherapy massage increased peripheral blood lymphocytes, CD8+, and CD16+ cells compared with carrier-oil massage in 11 healthy adults.
studies.limitations: n=11; preliminary; blend also contained cypress and sweet marjoram oils.
studies.title: Immunological and Psychological Benefits of Aromatherapy Massage

studies.authors: Shiina Y, Funabashi N, Lee K, Toyoda T, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy reduced serum cortisol and improved coronary flow velocity reserve in healthy men.
studies.limitations: Small sample; acute effects only; healthy men.
studies.title: Relaxation effects of lavender aromatherapy improve coronary flow velocity reserve in healthy men evaluated by transthoracic Doppler echocardiography

studies.authors: Ghaderi F, Solhjou N
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy during dental treatment lowered salivary cortisol, pulse rate, and injection pain scores in children aged 7 to 9.
studies.limitations: n=24 crossover; pediatric dental setting only.
studies.title: The effects of lavender aromatherapy on stress and pain perception in children during dental treatment: A randomized clinical trial

studies.authors: Bikmoradi A, Seifi Z, Poorolajal J, Araghchian M, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: lavender inhalation aromatherapy had no significant effect on mental stress or vital signs after coronary bypass surgery, except for systolic blood pressure.
studies.limitations: n=60; single center; two-day intervention only.
studies.title: Effect of inhalation aromatherapy with lavender essential oil on stress and vital signs in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery: A single-blinded randomized clinical trial
Clove oil reverses learning and memory deficits in scopolamine-treated mice
studies.authors: Halder S, Mehta AK, Kar R, Mustafa M, Mediratta PK, Sharma KK
studies.finding: In scopolamine-treated mice, repeated clove-oil pretreatment significantly reversed measures of acquisition and retention memory impairment in elevated-plus-maze and passive-avoidance tasks.
studies.limitations: Mouse model using injected clove oil and pharmacologically induced memory impairment; does not establish cognitive benefit in humans or from normal aromatic use.

studies.title: Acute effect of essential oil of Eugenia caryophyllata on cognition and pain in mice
studies.authors: Halder S, Mehta AK, Mediratta PK, Sharma KK
studies.finding: Acute clove-oil administration significantly improved scopolamine-induced retention-memory deficits in mice at tested doses; the study also evaluated analgesic effects.
studies.limitations: Mouse model with intraperitoneal administration and scopolamine-induced impairment; not evidence of human cognitive enhancement.

studies.title: Effects of Eugenol on Memory Performance, Neurogenesis, and Dendritic Complexity of Neurons in Mice Analyzed by Behavioral Tests and Golgi Staining of Brain Tissue
studies.authors: Irie Y, et al.
studies.finding: Oral eugenol increased spatial and recognition-memory measures in mice and was associated with increased neurogenesis and dendritic complexity in hippocampal regions, although Morris-water-maze escape latency was not significantly changed.
studies.limitations: Small mouse study of isolated eugenol; findings do not establish cognitive benefit in humans or from clove-oil aroma.

studies.title: Treatment of dandruff with 5% tea tree oil shampoo
studies.authors: Satchell AC, Saurajen A, Bell C, Barnetson RSC
studies.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
studies.finding: In a randomized trial, 5% tea tree oil shampoo improved the dandruff severity score by 41% versus 11% with placebo after four weeks.
studies.limitations: Specific 5% shampoo formulation; results do not establish effects of other tea-tree products.

studies.title: The efficacy of 5% topical tea tree oil gel in mild to moderate acne vulgaris: a randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled study
studies.authors: Enshaieh S, Jooya A, Siadat AH, Iraji F
studies.journal: Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology
studies.finding: In 60 participants, 5% tea tree oil gel produced significantly greater improvement in acne lesion counts and severity than placebo over 45 days.
studies.limitations: Specific topical gel and acne population; does not establish efficacy of diluted sprays or other formulations.

studies.title: Effects of Rosmarinus officinalis L. on memory performance, anxiety, depression, and sleep quality in university students: A randomized clinical trial
studies.authors: Nematolahi P, Mehrabani M, Karami-Mohajeri S, Dabaghzadeh F
studies.finding: Oral rosemary powder for one month was associated with improvements in prospective and retrospective memory, anxiety, depression and several sleep-quality measures versus placebo.
studies.limitations: Studied oral rosemary powder, not rosemary essential oil or inhalation.

studies.title: Effectiveness of lemon essential oil in reducing test anxiety in nursing students
studies.authors: Bahçecik N, et al.
studies.finding: Fifteen minutes of lemon essential-oil inhalation reduced test-anxiety scores in nursing students compared with control.
studies.limitations: Small student sample and acute exposure; does not establish treatment of anxiety disorders.

studies.title: Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Effects of Different Samples of Five Commercially Available Essential Oils
studies.authors: Neagu R, Popovici V, Ionescu LE, Ordeanu V, Popescu DM, Ozon EA, Gird CE
studies.finding: Commercial oregano, eucalyptus, rosemary, clove and peppermint oil samples showed antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against tested S. aureus, E. coli and P. aeruginosa, with substantial sample-to-sample variation.
studies.limitations: In-vitro sample- and concentration-dependent effects, often weak or undetected at lower dilutions. Biofilm-formation testing does not establish mature-biofilm removal, cleaning or disinfection.

studies.title: Lavender, tea tree and lemon oils as antimicrobials in washing liquids and soft body balms
studies.authors: Kunicka-Styczyńska A, Sikora M, Kalemba D
studies.finding: Lavender, tea tree and lemon essential oils were evaluated as antimicrobial ingredients in washing liquid and body-balm formulations against bacteria and Candida.
studies.limitations: Formulation-specific laboratory testing; not finished Sunny's Shield evidence.

studies.title: Chemical Composition and Antibacterial Activity of Liquid and Volatile Phase of Essential Oils against Planktonic and Biofilm-Forming Cells of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
studies.authors: Brożyna M, et al.
studies.finding: Across seven oils tested against P. aeruginosa, liquid and volatile rosemary and tea tree oils showed notable antibiofilm activity in the reported assays.
studies.limitations: In-vitro study; activity differed between liquid and vapor phases and cannot be extrapolated to clinical efficacy.

studies.title: The Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm In Vitro Activity of Liquid and Vapour Phases of Selected Essential Oils against Staphylococcus aureus
studies.authors: Brożyna M, et al.
studies.finding: Liquid and vapor phases of selected essential oils were tested against 16 biofilm-forming S. aureus strains, demonstrating oil- and phase-dependent antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity.
studies.limitations: Laboratory biofilm models only; effectiveness varied substantially by oil and assay.

studies.title: Comparative analysis of essential oil efficacy against the Asian longhorned tick Haemaphysalis longicornis (Acari: Ixodidae)
studies.authors: Kim D, et al.
studies.finding: Clove, eucalyptus, lavender and mint oils showed concentration-dependent acaricidal and repellent activity against Asian longhorned ticks; clove performed strongly in the reported assays.
studies.limitations: Laboratory/host-attachment model against one tick species; not a human-use repellent trial.

studies.title: Repellent activity of essential oils to the Lone Star tick, Amblyomma americanum
studies.authors: Bissinger BW, et al.
studies.finding: In contact repellency assays against Lone Star tick nymphs, clove ranked highest among the natural oils tested, with oregano and peppermint also evaluated.
studies.limitations: Bioassay evidence against one tick species; does not establish duration or safety of a consumer repellent formulation.

studies.title: Efficacy of plant extracts and oils as mosquito repellents
studies.authors: Jaenson TGT, Pålsson K, Borg-Karlson AK
studies.finding: Laboratory and field testing of multiple natural products found good mosquito repellency for several extracts and oils, including eucalyptus, with activity varying by product and mosquito species.
studies.limitations: Older comparative repellent work with heterogeneous natural products; formulation and exposure details limit direct product comparisons.

studies.title: Cutaneous application of menthol 10% solution as an abortive treatment of migraine without aura: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossed-over study
studies.authors: Borhani Haghighi A, et al.
studies.finding: In a crossover study of 35 patients and 118 migraine attacks, topical 10% menthol solution was evaluated for pain-free and pain-relief migraine endpoints versus a low-concentration control.
studies.limitations: Tested isolated menthol solution rather than peppermint oil; small crossover study.

studies.title: Concomitant therapy with Cineole (Eucalyptole) reduces exacerbations in COPD: a placebo-controlled double-blind trial
studies.authors: Worth H, Schacher C, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: In 242 patients with stable COPD, six months of oral cineole adjunct therapy reduced the combined frequency, severity and duration of exacerbations compared with placebo.
studies.limitations: Oral purified cineole adjunct therapy, not eucalyptus oil or inhaled use.

studies.title: Therapy for acute nonpurulent rhinosinusitis with cineole: results of a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
studies.authors: Kehrl W, Sonnemann U, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: Oral cineole produced significantly greater reductions in a rhinosinusitis symptom-sum score than placebo after four and seven days.
studies.limitations: Purified oral cineole, not eucalyptus essential oil or topical/inhaled use.

studies.title: Efficacy of cineole in patients suffering from acute bronchitis: a placebo-controlled double-blind trial
studies.authors: Fischer J, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: A multicenter placebo-controlled trial evaluated 600 mg/day oral cineole for ten days in 242 patients with acute bronchitis and reported faster improvement in bronchitis symptoms.
studies.limitations: Purified oral cineole; not evidence for eucalyptus-oil spray or inhalation.

studies.title: Patients with asthma benefit from concomitant therapy with cineole: a placebo-controlled, double-blind trial
studies.authors: Worth H, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: In 247 asthma patients, six months of oral cineole adjunct therapy was evaluated for lung function, asthma symptoms and quality of life versus placebo.
studies.limitations: Purified oral cineole as adjunct therapy; not eucalyptus essential oil and not a replacement for asthma treatment.

studies.title: Carvacrol improves pulmonary function tests, oxidant/antioxidant parameters and cytokine levels in asthmatic patients: A randomized, double-blind, clinical trial
studies.authors: Ghorani V, Alavinezhad A, Rajabi O, Boskabady MH
studies.finding: In 33 moderate asthma patients, oral carvacrol adjunct therapy improved respiratory symptoms, pulmonary-function measures and several inflammatory/oxidative markers versus baseline and placebo.
studies.limitations: Small trial of purified oral carvacrol used alongside routine asthma medication; not oregano oil.

studies.title: Possible therapeutic effect of carvacrol on asthmatic patients: A randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled, Phase II clinical trial
studies.authors: Alavinezhad A, Khazdair MR, Boskabady MH
studies.finding: In a small phase II trial, two months of oral carvacrol improved pulmonary-function measures and reduced several respiratory symptoms and inflammatory markers compared with placebo.
studies.limitations: Small study of purified oral carvacrol; not oregano essential oil.

studies.title: Safety and tolerability of carvacrol in healthy subjects: a phase I clinical study
studies.authors: Ghorani V, et al.
studies.finding: One month of oral carvacrol at 1 or 2 mg/kg/day was generally tolerated in healthy subjects; measured laboratory values remained within normal ranges despite several statistically significant changes.
studies.limitations: Safety/tolerability study of purified oral carvacrol, not evidence of oregano-oil efficacy.

studies.title: Tea tree oil: a systematic review of randomized clinical trials
studies.authors: Ernst E, Huntley A
studies.finding: A systematic review located four randomized trials and judged tea-tree-oil evidence for acne and fungal infections promising but not compelling at that time.
studies.limitations: Older review with only four trials; later studies should be considered separately.

studies.title: The effect of cinnamon supplementation on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: An updated systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
studies.authors: Moridpour AH, Kavyani Z, Khosravi S, et al.
studies.finding: Across 24 RCTs, cinnamon supplementation significantly reduced fasting blood sugar, HOMA-IR, and HbA1c versus control, with no significant change in serum insulin.
studies.limitations: Heterogeneous oral cinnamon preparations and doses across trials. Secondary evidence does not support metabolic effects of cinnamon essential oil or a spray.
studies.material: Oral cinnamon supplements in a systematic review; not cinnamon bark essential oil.

studies.title: Plasma 1,8-cineole correlates with cognitive performance following exposure to rosemary essential oil aroma
studies.authors: Moss M, Oliver L
studies.finding: Higher blood 1,8-cineole levels after rosemary aroma exposure correlated with better speed and accuracy on cognitive tasks, with no speed-accuracy trade-off.
studies.limitations: Correlational design, n=20, single exposure session.

studies.title: Short-term study on the effects of rosemary on cognitive function in an elderly population
studies.authors: Pengelly A, Snow J, Mills SY, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED DOSE RESPONSE: 750 mg dried rosemary leaf improved speed of memory in older adults, while 6000 mg significantly impaired cognitive performance and alertness.
studies.limitations: Dried leaf powder, not essential oil; acute single-dose effects only.

studies.title: Effect of aromatherapy on symptoms of dysmenorrhea in college students: a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial
studies.authors: Han SH, Hur MH, Buckle J, et al.
studies.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
studies.finding: Topical aromatherapy with a lavender, clary sage, and rose blend significantly reduced menstrual cramp severity versus placebo.
studies.limitations: Topical lavender, clary sage and rose blend; individual oil contributions were not isolated. No arbitrary spray or single-oil efficacy inference.

studies.title: Anti-Plaque and Anti-Gingivitis Efficacy of 0.25% Lemongrass Oil and 0.2% Chlorhexidine Mouthwash in Children
studies.authors: Akula S, Nagarathna J, Srinath K
studies.finding: 0.25% lemongrass oil mouthwash reduced plaque and gingival indices in children comparably to 0.2% chlorhexidine over 21 days.
studies.limitations: n=60 children; 21-day follow-up; no adult data.

studies.title: Aromatherapy for pain management in labour
studies.authors: Smith CA, Collins CT, Crowther CA
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: across 2 trials (535 women), aromatherapy showed no difference versus control for labor pain intensity, assisted vaginal birth, or caesarean section.
studies.limitations: Only 2 trials; authors concluded evidence is insufficient for practice recommendations.

studies.title: Aromatherapy with peppermint, isopropyl alcohol, or placebo is equally effective in relieving postoperative nausea
studies.authors: Anderson LA, Gross JB
studies.finding: NULL RESULT for peppermint: nausea scores fell equally with peppermint, isopropyl alcohol, and saline placebo; authors attributed relief to controlled breathing rather than aroma.
studies.limitations: n=33; saline placebo equally effective, suggesting non-specific effects.

studies.title: Treatment of interdigital tinea pedis with 25% and 50% tea tree oil solution: a randomized, placebo-controlled, blinded study
studies.authors: Satchell AC, Saurajen A, Bell C, et al.
studies.finding: In 158 patients, tea tree oil solution improved clinical symptoms of interdigital tinea pedis versus placebo in a blinded RCT.
studies.limitations: Symptom improvement exceeded mycological cure rates.

studies.title: Evaluation of Antibacterial Activity in Some Algerian Essential Oils and Selection of Thymus vulgaris as a Potential Biofilm and Quorum Sensing Inhibitor Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
studies.authors: Mohammed Aggad FZ, Ilias F, Elghali F, et al.
studies.finding: Thyme oil rich in thymol inhibited biofilm formation and quorum-sensing virulence factors in a hospital Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain, with docking data suggesting thymol and carvacrol bind its quorum-sensing receptors.
studies.limitations: In-vitro only; single hospital strain.

studies.title: Antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of thyme oil, oregano oil, and their combination against Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii polymicrobial biofilms
studies.authors: Anees TMM, Suchithra KV, Shetty AV, et al.
studies.finding: Thyme and oregano oils acted synergistically to disrupt dual-species Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii biofilms by over 90%, downregulating biofilm-associated genes.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; no human data.

studies.title: Essential oils of Pinus sylvestris, Citrus limon and Origanum vulgare exhibit high bactericidal and anti-biofilm activities against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Streptococcus suis
studies.authors: Jurado P, Uruen C, Martinez S, et al.
studies.finding: Scots pine and lemon oils showed strong bactericidal and biofilm-dispersal activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, attributed to alpha/beta-pinene and limonene acting on the bacterial outer membrane.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; clinical relevance untested.

studies.title: Innovative antifungal strategies: enhanced biofilm inhibition of Candida albicans by a modified tea tree oil formulation
studies.authors: Tuan DA, Uyen PVN, Khuon NV, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil inhibited Candida albicans biofilm formation but could not eradicate more than 50 percent of mature biofilm at the concentrations tested.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; mature-biofilm eradication not achieved.

studies.title: Antibiofilm efficacy of tea tree oil and of its main component terpinen-4-ol against Candida albicans
studies.authors: Francisconi RS, Huacho PMM, Tonon CC, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil and terpinen-4-ol interfered with Candida albicans biofilm formation in a 60-second rinse simulation, supporting potential use in oral candidiasis.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; brief-exposure model only.

studies.title: In vitro antiviral activity of Melaleuca alternifolia essential oil
studies.authors: Garozzo A, Timpanaro R, Bisignano B, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil and terpinen-4-ol inhibited influenza A H1N1 replication below cytotoxic doses, with no virucidal activity and no effect on the other viruses tested.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; influenza only among the viruses screened.

studies.title: Screening of the essential oil effects on human H1N1 influenza virus infection: an in vitro study in MDCK cells
studies.authors: Najar B, Nardi V, Stincarelli MA, et al.
studies.finding: Among 19 oils screened, eucalyptus and rosemary oils showed anti-H1N1 activity with low cytotoxicity, with eucalyptol correlating positively with cell viability.
studies.limitations: In-vitro screening; no human data.

studies.title: Virucidal Activity of Lemon Essential Oil against Feline Calicivirus Used as Surrogate for Norovirus
studies.authors: Pellegrini F, Camero M, Catella C, et al.
studies.finding: Lemon essential oil significantly reduced feline calicivirus infectivity, a cultivable surrogate for human norovirus, suggesting surface-sanitizing potential.
studies.limitations: Surrogate virus in-vitro; not tested against human norovirus.

studies.title: Antiviral efficacy and mechanisms of action of oregano essential oil and its primary component carvacrol against murine norovirus
studies.authors: Gilling DH, Kitajima M, Torrey JR, et al.
studies.finding: Carvacrol inactivated murine norovirus within one hour by disrupting the viral capsid, outperforming oregano oil and suggesting use as a surface sanitizer.
studies.limitations: Surrogate virus in-vitro; high concentrations required.

studies.title: Antifungal activity of volatile compounds generated by essential oils against fungi commonly causing deterioration of bakery products
studies.authors: Guynot ME, Ramos AJ, Seto L, et al.
studies.finding: Vapours of cinnamon, clove, lemongrass, and thyme oils completely inhibited bakery-spoilage molds including Aspergillus and Penicillium species.
studies.limitations: Vapour-phase lab model; efficacy dropped in real food matrices.

studies.title: Highly Durable Antibacterial Properties of Cellulosic Fabric via beta-Cyclodextrin/Essential Oils Inclusion Complex
studies.authors: Farouk A, Sharaf S, Refaie R, et al.
studies.finding: Cotton fabric treated with cyclodextrin-encapsulated lavender, lemon, and rosemary oils retained antibacterial activity through multiple wash cycles.
studies.limitations: Textile-finishing lab study; no worn-garment testing.

studies.title: Antibacterial activity and interactions of plant essential oil combinations against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria
studies.authors: Semeniuc CA, Pop CR, Rotar AM, et al.
studies.finding: NULL/MIXED RESULT: parsley and lovage oils showed no inhibition against any tested bacteria, and most thyme-oil combinations were antagonistic rather than synergistic.
studies.limitations: Food-bacteria panel only; disc-diffusion screening.

studies.title: In vitro insecticidal and repellent activity of Cymbopogon essential oils and geraniol against cat flea.
studies.authors: de Oliveira Chaves JK, Campos DR, Santos Soares EFM, et al.
studies.finding: Geraniol showed the lowest LC50 values against cat flea eggs, pupae, adults, and whole life-cycle inhibition, while Cymbopogon martinii (palmarosa) oil was most potent against larvae and kept repellency at 90% or higher for 48 hours.
studies.limitations: Off-animal filter-paper assays; no pet treatment, host safety or field validation. The lemongrass arm was Cymbopogon flexuosus, not the catalog C. citratus. Each oil and geraniol arm must remain distinct.

studies.title: Insecticidal and Repellent Activity of Essential Oils from Copaifera reticulata, Citrus paradisi, Lavandula hybrida and Salvia sclarea Against Immature and Adult Stages of Ctenocephalides felis felis.
studies.authors: Lima EAS, Campos DR, Soares EFMS, et al.
studies.finding: All four oils showed insecticidal and repellent activity against cat flea life stages in vitro, with beta-caryophyllene-rich copaiba oil showing the strongest residual efficacy.
studies.limitations: In vitro only; Lavandula hybrida (lavandin) mapped to lavender; no host-animal testing.

studies.title: Acaricidal activity of Melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree) oil: in vitro sensitivity of sarcoptes scabiei var hominis to terpinen-4-ol.
studies.authors: Walton SF, McKinnon M, Pizzutto S, et al.
studies.finding: Five percent tea tree oil and its component terpinen-4-ol were highly effective at reducing scabies mite survival times in vitro, comparable to 5% permethrin and ivermectin.
studies.limitations: In vitro continuous-exposure assay; mites from a single crusted-scabies patient.

studies.title: In vitro activity of ten essential oils against Sarcoptes scabiei.
studies.authors: Fang F, Candy K, Melloul E, et al.
studies.finding: In contact assays 1% clove oil killed all scabies mites within 20 minutes and palmarosa within 50 minutes; efficacy order was clove, palmarosa, geranium, tea tree, then lavender.
studies.limitations: Mites from experimentally infected pigs; in vitro only.

studies.title: Biotoxicity of essential oil of Eucalyptus citriodora Hook (Myrtaceae) to dust mites.
studies.authors: Cai H, Xie P, Zhang X, et al.
studies.finding: Eucalyptus citriodora oil showed strong contact-fumigant toxicity to both house dust mite species, with citronellal the most toxic constituent and 100% vapor-phase mortality.
studies.limitations: Laboratory bioassays at high applied doses; no bedroom-scale testing.

studies.title: Repellent effect of oregano essential oil and carvacrol analogs against imported fire ants.
studies.authors: George G, Shah FM, Ali A, et al.
studies.finding: Oregano oil strongly repelled red and hybrid imported fire ants, with carvacrol (minimum repellent dose 0.98 ug/g) identified as the primary active constituent.
studies.limitations: Laboratory repellency assays; no field colony-level data.

studies.title: Common Home Remedies Do Not Deter Argentine Ants, Linepithema humile (Hymenoptera: Formicidae), from a Preferred Harborage.
studies.authors: Holloway JB, Suiter DR, Davis JW, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: tansy, cucumber, and soybean-extract home remedies failed to deter Argentine ants even at 4 to 10 times the recommended dose, while 1% peppermint oil was the most deterrent treatment and fresh rosemary and spearmint leaves also deterred harboring.
studies.limitations: Laboratory harborage assay; short 2 to 4 hour observation window.

studies.title: Comparative repellency of 38 essential oils against mosquito bites.
studies.authors: Trongtokit Y, Rongsriyam Y, Komalamisra N, et al.
studies.finding: Of 38 oils screened on human forearms, only undiluted citronella, patchouli, clove, and makaen oils gave 2 hours of complete repellency against Aedes aegypti, with clove lasting longest (2 to 4 hours) across three mosquito species; no oil at 10 to 50% lasted 2 hours.
studies.limitations: Small volunteer panel; laboratory forearm assay, not field conditions.

studies.title: Larvicidal activity of essential oil from Vitex negundo and Vitex trifolia on dengue vector mosquito Aedes aegypti.
studies.authors: Chandrasekaran T, Thyagarajan A, Santhakumari PG, et al.
studies.finding: Vitex trifolia and Vitex negundo oils killed Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus larvae at 50 to 125 ppm, with LC50 values around 51 to 58 ppm for Ae. aegypti.
studies.limitations: Laboratory larval assays; no field or non-target testing.

studies.title: Efficacy of Active Ingredients From the EPA 25(B) List in Reducing Attraction of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) to Humans.
studies.authors: Mitra S, Rodriguez SD, Vulcan J, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: rosemary oil showed no significant repellency against Aedes aegypti in the study's attraction assay, unlike peppermint oil which strongly reduced attraction at the first time point.
studies.limitations: Single laboratory assay design; short observation window.

studies.title: Experimental use of two standard tick collection methods to evaluate the relative effectiveness of several plant-derived and synthetic repellents against Ixodes scapularis and Amblyomma americanum (Acari: Ixodidae).
studies.authors: Schulze TL, Jordan RA, Dolan MC
studies.finding: In field-plot tick drags, nootkatone and a permethrin standard each repelled 100% of Ixodes scapularis nymphs through 14 days, slightly outperforming carvacrol (90.7%) and a plant-oil product (97.7%).
studies.limitations: Field-plot tick-drag evaluation. Isolated nootkatone and carvacrol are distinct from grapefruit and oregano essential oils; no arbitrary spray protection claim.

studies.title: Lemongrass essential oil and DEET inhibit attractant detection in infected and non-infected Ixodes scapularis ticks.
studies.authors: Gaudet K, Anholeto LA, Hillier NK, et al.
studies.finding: Exposure to lemongrass oil, citral, or geraniol significantly impaired adult female Ixodes scapularis ticks' ability to detect and respond to host attractant, regardless of pathogen infection status.
studies.limitations: Electrophysiology and Y-tube lab assays; behavioral disruption rather than bite prevention was measured.

studies.title: Effectiveness of aromatherapy with sweet orange oil (Citrus sinensis L.) in relieving pain and anxiety during labor.
studies.authors: Nascimento JC, et al.
studies.finding: Sweet orange inhalation significantly reduced labor pain intensity over time (p=0.0411) and anxiety (p<0.0001) versus a distilled-water placebo, while also lowering maternal blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate and fetal heart rate.
studies.limitations: Single-blind, single-center Brazilian trial; labor setting limits generalizability.

studies.title: Evaluation of the Anxiety-Reducing Effects of Aroma Stones with Bergamot Essential Oil before Examinations: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.authors: Wakui N, et al.
studies.finding: Bergamot aroma stones used for 3 days before examinations significantly lowered state anxiety scores versus water-stone controls on all three days (Cohen's d > 0.8) with no reported adverse events.
studies.limitations: Open-label, single-center design; 57 students; short 3-day intervention.

studies.title: Relaxing effect of ylang ylang oil on humans after transdermal absorption.
studies.authors: Hongratanaworakit T, et al.
studies.finding: Transdermal ylang ylang oil significantly decreased blood pressure and increased skin temperature in 40 healthy volunteers, who also rated themselves calmer and more relaxed than the control group.
studies.limitations: Short-term transdermal exposure; no dose-response tested.

studies.title: Effect of Lavandula angustifolia and Cananga odorata on decrease of blood pressure in high blood pressure volunteers: A randomized controlled trial.
studies.authors: Napavichayanun S, et al.
studies.finding: Sticker pads containing lavender and ylang ylang oils worn for 14 days significantly reduced systolic blood pressure and pulse rate versus placebo in volunteers with high blood pressure, with no adverse reactions.
studies.limitations: 34 high-BP volunteers in efficacy phase; longer-term effects unknown.

studies.title: The antibacterial activity of geranium oil against Gram-negative bacteria isolated from difficult-to-heal wounds.
studies.authors: Sienkiewicz M, et al.
studies.finding: Geranium oil inhibited the growth of Gram-negative clinical strains isolated from difficult-to-heal wounds, suggesting it may be a useful component of therapy against resistant wound pathogens.
studies.limitations: In vitro study only; clinical wound efficacy and safety not tested.

studies.title: Evaluation of Essential Oils and Extracts of Rose Geranium and Rose Petals as Natural Preservatives in Terms of Toxicity, Antimicrobial, and Antiviral Activity.
studies.authors: Androutsopoulou C, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: 5% rose geranium essential oil showed no antibacterial activity (though 100% oil was strongly effective against E. coli), while it and the rose geranium extracts showed antifungal activity against Aspergillus niger and dose-dependent antiviral activity, with no toxicity at tested dilutions.
studies.limitations: In vitro study only; antibacterial efficacy highly concentration-dependent.

studies.title: Underutilized Plant Cymbopogan martinii Derived Essential Oil Is Excellent Source of Bioactives with Diverse Biological Activities.
studies.authors: Amrita, et al.
studies.finding: Palmarosa essential oil, with geraniol as its major component, showed antibacterial, antifungal, anti-inflammatory and alpha-amylase-inhibitory (antidiabetic) activity in vitro along with strong antioxidant capacity.
studies.limitations: In vitro and biochemical assays only; no animal or human data.

studies.title: Chemical Composition and Anti-Lung Cancer Activities of Melaleuca quinquenervia Leaf Essential Oil: Integrating Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC/MS) Profiling, Network Pharmacology, and Molecular Docking.
studies.authors: Fikry E, et al.
studies.finding: Niaouli leaf essential oil (1,8-cineole 31.57%, alpha-pinene isomers 21.26%) showed selective cytotoxicity against A549 lung cancer cells (IC50 18.09 ug/mL), inhibited cell migration, and induced apoptosis and G0-G1 cell-cycle arrest.
studies.limitations: Cell-culture and computational research; no in-vivo or human efficacy. Cytotoxicity does not establish immune support or a therapeutic blend use.

studies.title: Metabolomics analysis to evaluate the antibacterial activity of the essential oil from the leaves of Cinnamomum camphora (Linn.) Presl.
studies.authors: Chen J, et al.
studies.finding: Cinnamomum camphora leaf essential oil showed anti-MRSA activity (MIC 0.8 mg/mL, MBC 1.6 mg/mL), damaging bacterial cell membranes and disrupting amino acid metabolism according to GC-MS metabolomics.
studies.limitations: In vitro study only; chemotype-dependent composition may vary.

studies.title: Frankincense oil derived from Boswellia carteri induces tumor cell specific cytotoxicity.
studies.authors: Frank MB, et al.
studies.finding: Frankincense oil suppressed viability of J82 bladder transitional carcinoma cells but not normal urothelial cells, activating genes for cell-cycle arrest, growth suppression and apoptosis.
studies.limitations: Boswellia carteri oil in bladder-cell cultures, not the catalog Boswellia serrata. Cell cytotoxicity is neither immune support nor clinical cancer or skin efficacy.

studies.title: Effect of essential oils prepared from Thai culinary herbs on sessile Candida albicans cultures.
studies.authors: Hovijitra RS, et al.
studies.finding: Cinnamon bark essential oil was potently fungicidal against both planktonic and sessile (biofilm) Candida albicans, though sessile MICs were 8 to 16 times higher than planktonic MICs.
studies.limitations: In vitro study only; much higher concentrations needed against biofilms than planktonic cells.

studies.title: Bactericidal activity of Myrrh extracts and two dosage forms against standard bacterial strains and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates with GC/MS profiling.
studies.authors: Khalil N, et al.
studies.finding: Myrrh essential oil achieved greater than 99.999% killing of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa within 2 hours, showed bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates, and a 5% myrrh mouthwash killed about 99.999% of S. aureus in saliva within 30 minutes.
studies.limitations: In vitro study only; cytotoxicity data limited to cell lines.

studies.title: The effect of lavender essential oil on anxiety level in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery: A double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
studies.authors: Seifi Z, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: Lavender essential oil inhalation produced no statistically significant difference in anxiety scores versus a distilled-water placebo in patients after coronary artery bypass graft surgery, although anxiety decreased in both groups.
studies.limitations: 60 patients; 2-day intervention in acute post-surgical setting; results may not generalize.

studies.title: Modulation of cognitive performance and mood by aromas of peppermint and ylang-ylang
studies.authors: Moss M, Hewitt S, Moss L, Wesnes K
studies.finding: In 144 healthy adults, peppermint aroma improved memory and subjective alertness. Ylang-ylang aroma increased calmness but reduced alertness, impaired memory and slowed processing.
studies.limitations: Single acute laboratory exposure with expectancy and scent-masking limitations; no treatment or finished-product performance claim.

studies.title: The effects of massage with frankincense and myrrh oil in chronic low back pain: A three-arm randomised controlled trial
studies.authors: Özdemir Alkanat H, Özdemir Ü, Kulaklı F
studies.finding: Twice-weekly massage using frankincense and myrrh essential oils produced greater reductions in pain and disability scores than jojoba-oil massage or no massage in adults with chronic low back pain.
studies.limitations: Combination intervention; cannot separate effects of frankincense from myrrh, and massage is a co-intervention.

studies.title: The effect of back massage with frankincense and myrrh oil before the cardiac electrophysiological procedure on back pain intensity and comfort: A single-blind randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Özdemir Ü, Taşcı S, Döner A, Özdemir Alkanat H, İnanç MT
studies.finding: Frankincense-and-myrrh aromatherapy massage increased several comfort measures versus comparator groups, but post-procedure pain scores did not significantly differ between groups.
studies.limitations: Mixed result; combination oils plus massage prevents attribution to either oil alone. Authors called for more rigorous pain research.

studies.title: Cancer-Related Fatigue: A Pilot Study Evaluating the Effect of Frankincense Essential Oil in Patients With Cancer Receiving Chemotherapy
studies.authors: Reis D, et al.
studies.finding: Frankincense oil applied to the feet around chemotherapy did not significantly reduce cancer-related fatigue compared with carrier-oil control.
studies.limitations: Pilot trial; negative result. Topical-foot application and oncology population limit generalization.

studies.title: Episiotomy wound healing by Commiphora myrrha (Nees) Engl. and Boswellia carteri Birdw. in primiparous women: A randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Faraji A, Aghdaki M, Hessami K, et al.
studies.finding: Among 90 women, myrrh-extract sitz baths improved episiotomy REEDA healing scores more than frankincense extract or betadine. Frankincense and betadine did not differ significantly.
studies.limitations: Specific extract preparations and postpartum clinical setting; no whole-oil or spray inference. Frankincense was Boswellia carteri, not the catalog Boswellia serrata.
studies.material: Separate myrrh and frankincense botanical-extract sitz baths, not essential oils.

studies.title: Aromatherapy effects on pain and anxiety during transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy: A randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Aydınlı B, et al.
studies.finding: In 120 men undergoing prostate biopsy, lavender and frankincense aromatherapy delivered by nebulizer were compared with placebo for procedural anxiety and pain.
studies.limitations: Procedure-specific clinical setting; separate oil groups should be interpreted from the full paper before making comparative claims.

studies.title: Cannabis sativa terpenes are cannabimimetic and selectively enhance cannabinoid activity
studies.authors: LaVigne JE, Hecksel R, Keresztes A, Streicher JM
studies.finding: Selected terpenes found in Cannabis sativa produced cannabinoid-like behavioral effects in mice and interacted with cannabinoid signaling in experimental models.
studies.limitations: Preclinical mouse and cellular work on selected isolated terpenes; does not establish effects of cannabis aroma, essential oil, or a finished product in humans.

studies.title: Terpene Synthases and Terpene Variation in Cannabis sativa
studies.authors: Booth JK, Bohlmann J
studies.finding: Reviews the diverse monoterpenes and sesquiterpenes produced by Cannabis sativa and the terpene synthases underlying cultivar-dependent aroma profiles.
studies.limitations: Plant chemistry review, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy.

studies.title: Terpenes in Cannabis sativa - From plant genome to humans
studies.authors: Booth JK, Page JE, Bohlmann J
studies.finding: Reviews Cannabis sativa terpene biosynthesis, genetic diversity, ecological roles, and potential relevance of volatile terpenes to human exposure.
studies.limitations: Narrative plant-science review; potential human relevance should not be interpreted as demonstrated clinical benefit.

studies.title: Minor, Nonterpenoid Volatile Compounds Drive the Aroma Differences of Exotic Cannabis
studies.authors: Oswald IW, et al.
studies.finding: Chemical and sensory analysis showed that cannabis aroma differences cannot be explained by dominant terpenes alone; minor volatile compounds make important contributions.
studies.limitations: Thirty-one ice-hash rosin extracts; not steam-distilled essential oil, efficacy evidence or a finished-product analysis.
studies.material: Ice-hash rosin extracts

studies.title: The phytochemical diversity of commercial Cannabis in the United States
studies.authors: Smith CJ, et al.
studies.finding: Large-scale chemical profiling of commercial Cannabis samples demonstrated substantial phytochemical diversity and showed that conventional strain labels poorly capture underlying chemistry.
studies.limitations: Commercial-sample chemistry study; not clinical evidence and includes cannabinoids as well as volatile chemistry.

studies.title: Identification of a New Family of Prenylated Volatile Sulfur Compounds in Cannabis Revealed by Comprehensive Two-Dimensional Gas Chromatography
studies.authors: Oswald IWH, et al.
studies.finding: Chemical analysis and sensory assessment associated prenylthiol with skunky aroma in the cannabis flowers and concentrated extracts studied.
studies.limitations: Flowers from 13 cultivars and three hydrocarbon extracts, plus a plant-development series. Not a steam-distilled oil analysis or efficacy study.
studies.material: Flowers and hydrocarbon extracts

studies.title: Nonterpenoid Chemical Diversity of Cannabis Phenotypes Predicts Differentiated Aroma Characteristics
studies.authors: Paryani TR, et al.
studies.finding: Analytical and sensory comparisons linked minor nonterpenoid differences with aroma differences among sibling cannabis phenotypes.
studies.limitations: Five ice-water hash rosin extracts. Small analytical/sensory comparison, not distilled oil or product efficacy evidence.
studies.material: Ice-water hash rosin extracts

studies.title: Flavonoids in Cannabis sativa: Biosynthesis, Bioactivities, and Biotechnology
studies.authors: Bautista JL, Yu S, Tian L
studies.finding: Reviews the biosynthesis and research literature on cannflavins in Cannabis sativa.
studies.limitations: Review of plant compounds and experimental research, not a distilled-oil analysis or clinical evidence for the finished formula.
studies.material: Plant material and reviewed preparations

studies.title: Chemical Composition, Antifungal and Antibiofilm Activities of the Essential Oil of Mentha piperita L.
studies.authors: Saharkhiz Mohammad Jamal, Motamedi Marjan, Zomorodian Kamiar et al.
studies.finding: Menthyl acetate was reported in the study oil. The same hydrodistilled oil inhibited tested fungi and Candida biofilm formation in laboratory assays.
studies.limitations: One characterized hydrodistilled sample differs from the catalog steam-distillation label. No human fungal treatment or disinfection claim.
studies.material: Essential oil; Hydrodistilled air-dried flowering aerial parts of Mentha piperita, Fars, Iran

studies.title: Chemical Composition and Biological Activities of Eucalyptus globulus Essential Oil
studies.authors: Čmiková Natália, Galovičová Lucia, Schwarzová Marianna et al.
studies.finding: Isobutyl isobutyrate was reported in the commercial sample. The same commercial oil was tested in bacterial, fungal, biofilm and vapor-phase food-model assays.
studies.limitations: One commercial sample; laboratory and food matrices do not establish human skin treatment or cleaning. 1,8-cineole is a cyclic ether, not an epoxide.
studies.material: Essential oil; Commercial Hanus oil from fresh Eucalyptus globulus leaves cultivated in Spain

studies.title: Essential Oil of Cymbopogon nardus (L.) Rendle: A Strategy to Combat Fungal Infections Caused by Candida Species
studies.authors: De Toledo Luciani, Ramos Matheus, Spósito Larissa et al.
studies.finding: Citronellal was reported in this C. nardus sample. The same C. nardus oil inhibited many Candida isolates and mature biofilms, with variable susceptibility and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity.
studies.limitations: C. nardus differs from C. winterianus; sample preparation differs from the catalog label. Cytotoxicity occurred below some antifungal MICs; no clinical skin treatment or topical safety inference.
studies.material: Essential oil; Cymbopogon nardus leaves collected July 2013 in a Brazilian medicinal-plant garden

studies.title: Essential Oil Characterization of Thymus vulgaris from Various Geographical Locations
studies.authors: Satyal Prabodh, Murray Brittney, McFeeters Robert et al.
studies.finding: Linalyl acetate was measured in sample #1.
studies.limitations: Chemotype-specific findings. Literature profiles in the paper are not additional measured samples. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Four directly measured Thymus vulgaris chemotypes from France and Serbia, May 2015, air-dried aerial parts

studies.title: Antioxidant and Antibacterial Capacities of Origanum vulgare L. Essential Oil from the Arid Andean Region of Chile and its Chemical Characterization by GC-MS
studies.authors: Simirgiotis Mario J., Burton Daniel, Parra Felipe et al.
studies.finding: Linalyl acetate was reported in the studied regional profile.
studies.limitations: Regional oil profile, not universal oregano composition. Colorimetric total phenolics do not identify named flavonoids. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Dried flowering aerial parts of Origanum vulgare, Socoroma/Putre, Chile, November 2019

studies.title: Lemon grass (Cymbopogon citratus) essential oil as a potent anti-inflammatory and antifungal drugs
studies.authors: Boukhatem Mohamed Nadjib, Ferhat Mohamed Amine, Kameli Abdelkrim et al.
studies.finding: Geranyl acetate was reported in the study oil. The same oil inhibited fungal growth in culture and reduced experimentally induced mouse-ear edema.
studies.limitations: Fresh/dried feedstock reporting is inconsistent. Fungal cultures and topical mouse experiments are separate models; neither establishes human skin benefit or safe inhalation.
studies.material: Essential oil; Cymbopogon citratus leaf/aerial material, Chiffa/Blida, Algeria, May 2013

studies.title: Chemical Composition, Olfactory Evaluation and Antioxidant Effects of the Leaf Essential Oil of Corymbia citriodora (Hook) from China
studies.authors: Jirovetz Leopold, Bail Stefanie, Buchbauer Gerhard et al.
studies.finding: Citronellal was reported; the source has a numerical value but sample-specific extraction is not established, so no composition number is imported.
studies.limitations: General introduction on steam distillation does not establish preparation of this sample. Rutin/quercetin assay comparators are not oil constituents. Not a PMD-rich processed product. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Chinese Corymbia citriodora leaf oil, commercial product 800319, Kurt Kitzing

studies.title: GC/MS Analysis of the Volatile Constituents of Corymbia citriodora Hook. from Réunion Island
studies.authors: Vernin G. A., Parkanyi C., Cozzolino F. et al.
studies.finding: Citronellyl citronellate was reported as a trace constituent; no numerical amount was obtained.
studies.limitations: Trace ester reported; numerical concentration not available in the accessible abstract. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Corymbia citriodora leaf oil from Réunion Island

studies.title: Anti-Staphylococcal Activity of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Essential Oil against Planktonic and Biofilm Cells Isolated from Canine Otological Infections
studies.authors: Albuquerque Vinicius de Queiroz, Soares Maria Janeila Carvalho, Matos Maria Nágila Carneiro et al.
studies.finding: (E)-Cinnamaldehyde was reported in this bark-oil sample. The same bark oil showed antistaphylococcal and antibiofilm effects against canine-otitis isolates in vitro.
studies.limitations: C. zeylanicum is a synonym of C. verum. Canine-source cultures are not treated dogs; bark oil differs from leaf/root oils. No veterinary treatment or dermal suitability claim.
studies.material: Essential oil; Commercial Laszlo Cinnamomum zeylanicum stem-bark oil, manufacturer-reported Sri Lankan origin

studies.title: Analysis of Polyphenolic Composition of a Herbal Medicinal Product: Peppermint Tincture
studies.authors: Bodalska Agnieszka, Kowalczyk Adam, Włodarczyk Maciej et al.
studies.finding: Eriocitrin and luteolin-7-O-rutinoside were reported. Flavonoids cannot be attributed to the added oil fraction.
studies.limitations: Not an essential-oil finding. Any source quantities are not imported here and cannot be attributed to distilled oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Plant extract / infusion; 23 commercial peppermint tinctures from Polish pharmacies

studies.title: Characterization of Chemical Composition and Antioxidant Activity of Eucalyptus globulus Leaves under Different Extraction Conditions
studies.authors: Park Jae Yeon, Kim Ju Yeon, Son Yun Gon et al.
studies.finding: Epicatechin, isoquercitrin and quercitrin were reported in leaf extracts.
studies.limitations: Not an essential-oil finding. Any source quantities are not imported here and cannot be attributed to distilled oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Plant extract / infusion; Eucalyptus globulus leaves from Haman-gun, Republic of Korea

studies.title: Modulatory Impact of Lamiaceae Metabolites on Apoptosis of Human Leukemia Cells
studies.authors: Berdowska Izabela, Zieliński Bogdan, Matusiewicz Małgorzata et al.
studies.finding: Luteolin-7-O-beta-glucuronide and apigenin-7-O-beta-glucoside were reported. The paper did not show a clear apoptotic effect for common-thyme extract; no treatment claim is inferred.
studies.limitations: Not an essential-oil finding. Any source quantities are not imported here and cannot be attributed to distilled oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Plant extract / infusion; Commercial Polish Thymus vulgaris herb, aqueous polyphenol-enriched extracts

studies.title: UHPLC-DAD Characterization of Origanum vulgare L. from Atacama Desert Andean Region and Antioxidant, Antibacterial and Enzyme Inhibition Activities
studies.authors: Parra Claudio, Muñoz Patricio, Bustos Luis et al.
studies.finding: Luteolin, naringenin, rutin and apigenin were reported.
studies.limitations: Not an essential-oil finding. Any source quantities are not imported here and cannot be attributed to distilled oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Plant extract / infusion; Origanum vulgare from the Atacama Desert Andean region

studies.title: Chemical characterization and anti-inflammatory activity of luteolin glycosides isolated from lemongrass
studies.authors: Francisco Vera, Figueirinha Artur, Costa Gustavo et al.
studies.finding: Cynaroside and isoorientin were identified in the leaf-infusion research.
studies.limitations: Not an essential-oil finding. Any source quantities are not imported here and cannot be attributed to distilled oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence; biological results are not inferred from the title.
studies.material: Plant extract / infusion; Cymbopogon citratus leaf infusion and isolated glycosides

studies.title: Comparison of lemon oil composition after using different extraction methods
studies.authors: Gök Aslı, İsmail Kirbaşlar Ş., Gülay Kirbaşlar F.
studies.finding: Geranyl acetate was reported in the cold-pressed Kibris column.
studies.limitations: Cultivar-specific. Hydrodistilled and supercritical-extract columns are separate samples. This record summarizes chemical evidence, not efficacy inferred from the publication title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Kibris cultivar Citrus limon peel oil; cold-pressed comparison column

studies.title: Identification, Synthesis, and Characterization of Novel Sulfur-Containing Volatile Compounds from the In-Depth Analysis of Lisbon Lemon Peels (Citrus limon L. Burm. f. cv. Lisbon)
studies.authors: Cannon Robert J., Kazimierski Arkadiusz, Curto Nicole L. et al.
studies.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
studies.finding: Prenylthiol and a thiol-bearing acetate ester were identified in Lisbon peel extract. This leaves a gap for cold-pressed oil.
studies.limitations: Peel extract is not cold-pressed commercial lemon essential oil. This record summarizes chemical evidence, not efficacy inferred from the publication title.
studies.material: Peel solvent extract; Lisbon cultivar Citrus limon peel solvent extract

studies.title: Authenticity analysis of citrus essential oils by HPLC-UV-MS on oxygenated heterocyclic components
studies.authors: Fan Hao, Wu Qingli, Simon James E. et al.
studies.journal: Journal of Food and Drug Analysis
studies.finding: No direct positive PMF record for cold-pressed lemon oil is established by this curated source.
studies.limitations: Selected lemon samples lacked PMFs. Coumarins and furanocoumarins are not flavonoids; non-detection is not universal absence. This record summarizes chemical evidence, not efficacy inferred from the publication title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Authentic lemon and orange essential-oil profiles

studies.title: Authenticity Analysis of Cold-Pressed Orange Essential Oils by GC/MS on Polymethoxyflavone Components
studies.authors: Yang Kai-Min, Chen Chih-Wei, Chen Min-Hung et al.
studies.finding: Tangeretin, sinensetin and nobiletin were verified with standards in cold-pressed orange oils. Source quantities are not imported.
studies.limitations: Commercial, crude and compounded samples are separate; do not merge them into a typical range. This record summarizes chemical evidence, not efficacy inferred from the publication title.
studies.material: Essential oil: nonvolatile fraction; Commercial and crude cold-pressed orange oils, nonvolatile fraction

studies.title: The effects of different extraction methods on essential oils from orange and tangor: From the peel to the essential oil
studies.authors: Park Min Kyung, Cha Ji Yoon, Kang Min‐Cheol et al.
studies.finding: Neryl acetate (called nerol acetate in the paper) was reported in the cold-pressed orange comparison. No concentration is imported.
studies.limitations: Orange and tangor are distinct samples; enrichment versus hydrodistillation is not a universal quantity. This record summarizes chemical evidence, not efficacy inferred from the publication title.
studies.material: Essential oil; Cold-pressed Citrus sinensis orange peel oil, separate from tangor samples

chemicalGroups.label: Aldehydes
chemicalGroups.description: A fragrant functional group found across chemical families. Citral gives lemongrass its lemony character; cinnamaldehyde is associated with cinnamon.
chemicalGroups.details: An aldehyde contains a terminal carbonyl group (-CHO). Citral is a mixture of geranial and neral. Citral and citronellal remain monoterpenoids; cinnamaldehyde remains a phenylpropanoid.

chemicalGroups.label: Esters
chemicalGroups.description: Many volatile esters contribute floral or fruity notes. Linalyl acetate is an example associated with lavender and bergamot.
chemicalGroups.details: An ester functional group can overlap with a primary chemical family. Linalyl acetate is both a monoterpenoid and an acetate ester. Not all esters are volatile or fragrant.

chemicalGroups.label: Thiols
chemicalGroups.description: Some sulfur-containing volatiles affect aroma at trace levels. Examples have been reported in grapefruit oil and in cannabis flower or extract research.
chemicalGroups.details: Thiols contain a sulfur-hydrogen (-SH) group. Other volatile sulfur compounds include sulfides and thioesters, so not every sulfur volatile is a thiol.

chemicalGroups.label: Flavonoids
chemicalGroups.description: Typically nonvolatile plant polyphenols. They belong to broader plant chemistry and are not generally aroma molecules or dominant constituents of steam-distilled oils.
chemicalGroups.details: Cannflavins illustrate plant-material chemistry. Nobiletin is documented in nonvolatile fractions of some cold-pressed citrus oils. These findings stay separate from volatile fingerprints. LC/HPLC methods are commonly used for flavonoids.
